description.narrative: A National Framework for Daycare was agreed in June 2023 by the Government of Jordan in consultation with social partners and active civil society stakeholders. The National Framework for Daycare (2023-2025) was finalized in the context of an ILO-led regional conference on 'Care at Work: Investing in Care Leave Policies and Care Services for a more Gender-Equal World of Work'’. In conjunction with the regional conference, a regional report on Investing in Care was prepared highlighting the business case for investing in care in Jordan and in the MENA region. Furthermore, Jordan led an awareness campaign on maternity and paternity leave policies with the aim to advance legal and practical proposals on the implementation of international labour standards and decent work in the country. With financial support from the Government of Norway and the Swedish International Development Agency and in collaboration with UN Women, the ILO supported consultations on the National Framework for DayCare as well as coordination among stakeholders for the organization of a regional conference that facilitated the adoption of the above mentioned National Framework.

description.narrative: In March 2023, the government of Jordan adopted amendments to the Labour Law No. 10 whereby, in Article 29, the term "sexual harassment" is introduced with major penalties. and, in Article 6 has been amended to include the prohibition of gender based discrimination between employees. With the support from the Government of Norway and the Swedish International Development Agency, and in collaboration with UN Women, the ILO supported the Ministry of Labour in drafting the proposed amendments to the labour law to accompany the amendment made to law on equal pay in 2018/19. The ILO facilitated social dialogue sessions debating the labour law amendments and held a national briefing session for parliamentarians on ILS and gender equality to raise awareness on the importance of the proposed amendments. These efforts led to the eventual passage of the amendments.

description.narrative: In October 2022, the Social Security Corporation formally adopted amendments to the Maternity Insurance Regulations to permit a part of the Fund revenues to be used to subsidise working mothers’ childcare costs and operational costs of childcare providers. Furthermore, the Ministry of Social Development, the Ministry of Labour, and the Social Security Corporation have reviewed and updated the National Framework for Childcare in November 2022. With the support from the Government of Norway and the Swedish International Development Agency, t and in collaboration with UN Women, the ILO provided technical support to Ministry of Labour for the design of the scheme as part of COVID-related support measures to enable women to return to work by accessing childcare and childcare providers to restart operations after a long period of closures. Furthermore, the ILO supported Ministry of Labour in the design of the interventions of childcare provisions covered in the National Framework including a field visit to Norway to understand better the working of some of the models and in the consultations with stakeholders to review and revise the National Framework.

description.narrative: To ensure effective implementation of Convention No. 190, in April 2023 the National Labour Law was amended to include a provision on sexual harassment (Article 29), alongside sexual assault with clear definitions. The labour law reform has been the result of effective social dialogue. In 2021, the government of Jordan via the Joint National Commission for Women and the General Federation of Jordanian Trade Unions developed the National Strategy on Violence and Harassment in the World of Work, which reflects the government's intent to ratify C190. The strategy was endorsed by more than 50 stakeholders representing workers, employers and civil society organisations (CSOs) and is based on the main elements of prevention, response, and protection, as well as integrated policy and accountability mechanisms. It was published in the official gazette on 16 April 2023 and became effective a month later (16 May 2023). Through the support of the Norway and the Swedish International Development Agency, and in collaboration with UN Women, the ILO supported the constituents via the development of a gap analysis of the law vis-a-vis C190. The gap analysis served as a basis for tripartite consultations on the development of the national strategy as well as legislative reform. Technical and financial support was provided by the ILO to the gap analysis and consultations thereof.
